paragraphs: Evaluating a circuit layout quickly matters because placement and routing consume substantial time in physical circuit design. Existing learning approaches represent circuits either as handcrafted images or as graphs. The abstract identifies drawbacks in both: image representations depend on manual conversion choices, while graph representations require time-consuming preprocessing.

This paper instead treats circuit components as a set of points and applies Transformer-based methods developed for point-cloud perception. The model extracts features directly from raw circuit data without preprocessing. This also supports end-to-end training, allowing feature extraction and the prediction task to be learned together rather than separated by a handcrafted representation.

Experiments report state-of-the-art congestion prediction on CircuitNet and ISPD2015, together with state-of-the-art design rule violation prediction on CircuitNet. These findings support point-cloud representations as a useful alternative for the evaluated circuit analysis tasks. The broader contribution is a connection between point-cloud perception and electronic design automation, with released code and pretrained models supporting further research.
neurips-2023-circuit-as-set-of-points-e9.tldr: Representing circuit components as point clouds enables direct, end-to-end learning and achieves leading results on the evaluated circuit prediction tasks.

paragraphs: Sequential experiments can change treatment assignments as observations arrive, potentially improving the precision of causal estimates. This paper asks how closely an adaptive design can approach an ideal Neyman allocation. That benchmark is infeasible in practice because it has access to all potential outcomes, including outcomes that the experimenter cannot observe.

The authors connect this allocation problem to online optimization and introduce two equivalent measures, Neyman Ratio and Neyman Regret, for evaluating adaptive designs. Their Clip-OGD method achieves expected Neyman regret that grows at most on the order of the square root of the experiment length, apart from logarithmic factors. This guarantee implies recovery of the optimal Neyman variance in large samples.

The paper also constructs a conservative variance estimator to support asymptotically valid confidence intervals and supplements the theory with simulations using microeconomic experiment data. The contribution therefore covers both allocation efficiency and uncertainty estimation. Its precision guarantee concerns large-sample behavior, rather than exact equality with the ideal allocation in every finite experiment.
neurips-2023-clip-ogd-an-experimental-de.tldr: Clip-OGD adaptively allocates treatments with a regret guarantee that recovers ideal Neyman variance in large samples.

paragraphs: Text prompts can leave important aspects of an intended image ambiguous. Cocktail addresses this by adding multiple kinds of external control to text-conditioned diffusion generation. Its purpose is to combine those signals while also controlling where they influence the image, giving the generation process more specific direction than language alone provides.

The pipeline uses a generalized ControlNet, called gControlNet, to align signals from different modalities and introduce them into a pretrained diffusion model. This hypernetwork can receive combinations of modality signals simultaneously or incorporate additional signals through supplementary fusion. A controllable normalization mechanism, ControlNorm, combines the signals and injects them into the image-generation backbone.

Cocktail also introduces spatial guidance during sampling so that a control signal affects its designated region, addressing unwanted objects in the generated image. The reported demonstrations show high-quality synthesis that follows multiple external signals. Together, the components address two related requirements: combining different kinds of guidance and applying that guidance to the intended spatial locations.
neurips-2023-cocktail-mixing-multi-modal.tldr: Cocktail combines multiple control modalities and spatial guidance to steer text-conditioned diffusion images toward several external signals.

paragraphs: An instruction-following agent can receive useful teaching signals while people are interacting with it. This paper proposes and deploys a system that continually learns from those signals. Users give natural-language instructions and then provide binary feedback in real time as they watch the agent attempt to carry them out.

The learning method uses a contextual bandit formulation, converting feedback into immediate reward. This makes the feedback part of the training process rather than merely an evaluation collected after interaction. The approach connects what users observe during collaboration with subsequent improvement in instruction execution, using a simple feedback format that does not itself require a full demonstration.

Across thousands of human-agent interactions, instruction execution accuracy improves by 15.4 percentage points over time. The authors also report robustness to several design variations and find that the feedback provides a learning signal roughly equivalent to supervised demonstration data. These results support continual learning from realtime feedback in the evaluated setting, with the comparison to demonstrations remaining approximate.
neurips-2023-continual-learning-for-inst.tldr: An instruction-following agent learns continually from realtime binary user feedback, improving execution accuracy by 15.4 percentage points in the evaluation.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary segmentation requires identifying image regions and recognizing categories beyond a fixed label set. Existing approaches often first generate masks and then use CLIP to classify the masked content. This can require extracting image features multiple times, increasing the cost of an already demanding recognition task.

FC-CLIP shares one frozen convolutional CLIP backbone across a single-stage system. The approach rests on two observations: frozen CLIP features retain open-vocabulary recognition ability while supporting strong mask generation, and convolutional CLIP handles larger images than those used in its image-text pretraining. Sharing these features simplifies the pipeline while improving the reported accuracy-cost balance.

When trained only on COCO panoptic data and evaluated zero-shot, FC-CLIP improves results on ADE20K, Mapillary Vistas, and Cityscapes relative to the compared prior method under the same setting. It also reports 7.5 times faster training, 6.6 times faster testing, and 5.9 times fewer total parameters than that method. These results show that a shared frozen backbone can deliver both strong segmentation and substantial efficiency gains in the evaluated comparisons.
neurips-2023-convolutions-die-hard-open-.tldr: FC-CLIP shares a frozen convolutional CLIP backbone for mask generation and recognition, improving segmentation accuracy and efficiency in reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Labels on a graph can depend on one another, so predicting each node separately may overlook useful structure. This paper studies structured node classification, particularly when some labels are already known. The central aim is to use those known labels while modeling relationships among all the labels being predicted.

DPM-SNC learns a joint distribution over node labels through a reverse diffusion process. At prediction time, manifold-constrained sampling conditions its output on available labels. Because standard diffusion training does not directly address partially labeled data, the authors develop a training algorithm that maximizes a new variational lower bound, making the approach usable in that setting.

The paper also analyzes expressive power through AGG-WL, a proposed test that is strictly more powerful than the classic 1-WL test. This supplies a theoretical account of how diffusion can strengthen graph neural network classification. Experiments report advantages across partially labeled transductive tasks, inductive settings, and unlabeled graphs, supporting the framework across several forms of graph prediction.
neurips-2023-diffusion-probabilistic-mod.tldr: DPM-SNC uses diffusion to model node labels jointly and condition predictions on known labels, with theoretical and empirical support.

paragraphs: Deep spiking neural networks draw inspiration from biological signaling, but their training remains challenging. The paper identifies limitations in approaches that rely on pretraining and fine-tuning, indirect coding and reconstruction, or approximate gradients. It proposes EICIL as a learning framework organized around both excitatory and inhibitory behavior.

The key idea is to place these two behaviors within one training framework, drawing on how biological neurons transmit signals. According to the paper, their joint incorporation improves the biological resemblance and adaptability of spiking neuron models while expanding their representation space. The contribution therefore concerns how neurons behave during learning, as well as the overall method used to train the network.

Experiments compare EICIL with traditional learning approaches on multiple datasets, including CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, and report better performance. The findings support the importance of integrating both behaviors during training in the evaluated models. They connect the proposed biologically inspired learning design with improved task performance, without providing a numerical size for those improvements in the abstract.
neurips-2023-eicil-joint-excitatory-inhi.tldr: EICIL jointly incorporates excitatory and inhibitory behavior into deep spiking-network training and outperforms traditional methods in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Variational flows depend on numerical transformations for sampling, evaluating densities, and estimating the evidence lower bound, or ELBO. This paper shows empirically that errors in common flows can accumulate catastrophically. The computed forward transformation can depart substantially from the exact transformation, and the computed inverse may fail to recover its starting input.

Those failures threaten different parts of the calculation: forward errors affect samples, while inverse errors affect density and ELBO computations. Yet the authors observe that outputs can remain accurate enough for applications despite serious instability. They investigate this apparent tension by treating variational flows as chaotic dynamical systems and applying shadowing theory.

The analysis provides theoretical guarantees on errors in sampling, density evaluation, and ELBO estimation. The authors also develop and empirically test a diagnostic procedure for validating results from unstable flows. The contribution is a way to assess the consequences of numerical instability, rather than treating instability alone as proof that every resulting quantity is unusable.
neurips-2023-embracing-the-chaos-analysi.tldr: Shadowing theory helps explain why numerically unstable variational flows can remain useful and supports a practical diagnostic for their outputs.

paragraphs: Explaining a time-series prediction involves both locating influential signals and recognizing the temporal patterns they form. TimeX addresses these connected needs by training an interpretable surrogate to mimic a pretrained time-series model. Its goal is to make explanations reflect how that model behaves while organizing them into understandable patterns.

The central mechanism is model behavior consistency. It preserves relationships from the pretrained model's latent space in the latent space learned by TimeX. The method produces discrete attribution maps and also learns representations of explanations themselves. These representations can provide visual landmarks that group similar explanations, helping users recognize recurring temporal structures.

Evaluation covers eight synthetic and real-world datasets, with physiological time-series case studies providing additional examination. TimeX ranks highest or second-highest on every reported metric across those datasets relative to the evaluated baselines. The case studies suggest that its components can support faithful, interpretable surrogates. The contribution combines strong reported attribution performance with a way to compare explanations across examples.
neurips-2023-encoding-time-series-explan.tldr: TimeX learns attribution maps and an explanation space by preserving relationships in a pretrained time-series model's internal representations.

paragraphs: Fictitious play is a repeated-play procedure used in game theory and multi-agent reinforcement learning. For potential games, it is known to converge to a Nash equilibrium when all players follow it. That eventual convergence leaves a separate practical question: how long might the process need before it reaches equilibrium?

This paper establishes a worst-case lower bound for potential games, focusing on games in which players have identical payoffs. The authors prove that fictitious play can require time exponential in the number of strategies, even with only two players. They demonstrate this through a recursively constructed coordination game with a unique Nash equilibrium.

The construction also ensures that every approximate Nash equilibrium must lie close to the pure equilibrium in a specified distance measure. This further characterizes the game's equilibrium structure. The result shows that aligned payoffs, few players, and a unique equilibrium do not by themselves ensure fast fictitious play. It establishes that slow instances exist, rather than claiming exponential behavior for every potential game.
neurips-2023-exponential-lower-bounds-fo.tldr: Fictitious play can take exponential time to reach equilibrium even in two-player coordination games with identical payoffs and a unique equilibrium.

paragraphs: In federated learning, individual clients may hold samples from only some of the classes that the shared model must recognize. The paper studies this partially class-disjoint setting, where local training objectives can conflict with the global objective. It identifies problems involving poorly maintained separation for missing classes and unused representation space for classes that are present.

FedGELA addresses both perspectives through classifier geometry. Globally, it fixes the classifier as a simplex Equiangular Tight Frame, giving all classes equal geometric discrimination and avoiding inaccurate classifier updates. Locally, it adapts to each client's distribution and uses space associated with absent classes to better accommodate classes available on that client.

Experiments across a range of datasets report average improvements of 3.9% over FedAvg and 1.5% over the best baselines. The paper also provides convergence guarantees for both local and global learning. Together, these contributions support coordinating a shared class structure with local adaptation when clients do not individually contain the full set of classes.
neurips-2023-federated-learning-with-bil.tldr: FedGELA combines a fixed global classifier geometry with local adaptation to improve federated learning when clients contain only subsets of classes.

paragraphs: Tables have structure that a language model may not automatically respect. Cells belong to rows, columns, and a whole table, and reordering rows or columns can preserve the relevant table content. HyTrel builds these structural properties into a tabular language model instead of relying only on learning them from pretraining data.

The method represents cells as hypergraph nodes. It connects cells using three kinds of hyperedges: those belonging to the same row, the same column, and the entire table. Under certain conditions, the authors prove maximal invariance: HyTrel assigns identical representations exactly when two tables are identical up to permutation. This combines insensitivity to ordering with a guarantee against collapsing other distinctions under those conditions.

On four downstream tasks, HyTrel consistently outperforms competitive baselines with minimal pretraining. Qualitative analyses also show representations that incorporate structure at cell, row, column, and table levels. These findings support encoding table-specific structure directly into the model as a useful aid to representation learning.
neurips-2023-hytrel-hypergraph-enhanced-.tldr: HyTrel uses hypergraphs to encode table structure and permutation invariance, improving four downstream tasks with minimal pretraining.

paragraphs: High-dimensional support vector machines often need some mechanism to favor useful solutions among many possibilities. This paper develops an algorithm that obtains regularizing behavior without adding an explicit regularization penalty. It combines an over-parameterized hinge-loss formulation with gradient descent to estimate the underlying parameters of a sparse SVM.

Nesterov's smoothing method is a second central ingredient. The authors use it to improve computational efficiency, particularly for deciding when to stop and reducing computational complexity. Their theory shows that unregularized gradient descent can achieve a near-oracle statistical convergence rate when initialization, step size, and the smoothing parameter are chosen appropriately. The guarantee therefore depends on those choices.

Numerical experiments check the theoretical findings and compare the method with explicit regularization. The reported results illustrate advantages of combining gradient descent with over-parameterization in sparse SVMs. The main significance is that the optimization process itself can provide useful statistical control, with both a conditional theoretical guarantee and supporting numerical evidence.
neurips-2023-implicit-regularization-in-.tldr: An over-parameterized, smoothed SVM achieves near-oracle statistical convergence without explicit regularization under appropriate optimization choices.

paragraphs: A language model can help planning in two ways: suggesting what to do and supplying commonsense knowledge about the world. This paper combines those roles in LLM-MCTS, a planning algorithm built around Monte Carlo Tree Search. The goal is to make complex planning more effective by using language-model knowledge within an explicit search process.

The model's world knowledge supplies prior beliefs for reasoning, while its action policy acts as a heuristic that guides search. These components have different jobs: one informs the planner's understanding of the world, and the other helps it search efficiently. Experiments on complex, novel tasks report wide-margin improvements over MCTS alone and policies induced by GPT2 and GPT3.5.

Further analyses involving multiplication, travel planning, and object rearrangement suggest a minimum-description-length principle. When the world model has a substantially shorter description than the policy, model-based planning with an LLM is likely preferable to using it solely as a policy. This is presented as a guiding principle supported by the analyses, rather than a universal guarantee.
neurips-2023-large-language-models-as-co.tldr: LLM-MCTS combines language-model world knowledge and action guidance within tree search, improving planning on the evaluated complex tasks.

paragraphs: A sample can have several views and several labels, while some views and labels are missing. This paper tackles that combined setting with a neural framework that separates two kinds of representation. One channel captures information shared across views; the other captures information specific to an individual view.

Several training components support this separation. A cross-channel contrastive loss strengthens the semantic content of the two channels. A label-guided graph regularization loss uses available supervision to preserve geometric relationships among samples in the learned features. The method also randomly masks fragments of vector features to improve the encoders' learning ability, adapting a masking idea to this input format.

The framework is designed to accommodate arbitrary absences of views and labels while also working on complete data. The reported experiments support its effectiveness and improved performance. Its central contribution is a coordinated approach to shared information, view-specific information, sample relationships, and missing inputs, rather than a single representation that must carry all of those roles.
neurips-2023-masked-two-channel-decoupli.tldr: A two-channel framework separates shared and view-specific information to learn from multi-view, multi-label data with missing views and labels.

paragraphs: Code language models can struggle when completion requires knowledge of types or APIs defined elsewhere in a repository or library. Monitor-guided decoding gives these models access to assistance analogous to what static analysis provides developers in an IDE. A monitor uses that analysis to guide generation using repository context.

The authors construct PragmaticCode, a repository-level Java method-completion dataset. They evaluate monitors that enforce type-consistent object dereferences and find consistent improvements in compilation rates and agreement with reference code across model sizes. With monitoring, SantaCoder-1.1B exceeds the much larger text-davinci-003 model on compilation rate and next-identifier match in the reported comparison.

A further study examines generalization across Java, C#, and Rust, as well as constraints involving method argument counts and stateful API protocols. The work shows how repository-aware analysis can strengthen code generation during decoding. Its findings also demonstrate that, for the evaluated measures, a smaller model with this assistance can outperform a larger model.
neurips-2023-monitor-guided-decoding-of-.tldr: Monitor-guided decoding uses repository static analysis to improve code completion, sometimes enabling smaller models to outperform larger ones.

paragraphs: Evolutionary optimization is attracting interest for deep-learning problems such as non-differentiable operations and meta-learning with long inner loops. Hardware acceleration and compatible software have made distributed evaluation of candidate populations easier. However, the paper identifies a shortage of practical hyperparameter knowledge and benchmarking tailored to these applications.

NeuroEvoBench addresses that gap with a benchmark designed specifically for deep-learning uses of evolutionary optimization. It evaluates both traditional optimizers and meta-learned alternatives. Its investigation covers resource allocation, fitness shaping, normalization, regularization, and scalability, connecting optimizer evaluation to practical choices involved in running these methods.

The contribution is a shared basis for studying evolutionary optimizers in settings where classical evolutionary benchmarks offer limited guidance. The abstract does not name a universally best optimizer; its emphasis is systematic evaluation of the methods and their configuration. The benchmark is released under the Apache-2.0 license, making the evaluation resource available for further use and investigation.
neurips-2023-neuroevobench-benchmarking-.tldr: NeuroEvoBench benchmarks traditional and meta-learned evolutionary optimizers on deep-learning applications and investigates practical configuration choices.

paragraphs: Experiments often summarize a treatment using one average effect, but that summary can become uninformative when effects change over time. This paper studies experimental design under linear trends. It considers both learning the changing treatment effect and reducing welfare loss for participants while the experiment is running.

These objectives create competing demands on the experimental design. The authors propose an efficient design that can be configured for an optimal estimation error rate, an optimal regret rate, or a Pareto-optimal trade-off between them. The trade-off describes choices where improving one objective requires giving ground on the other, rather than expecting one configuration to optimize both independently.

Information-theoretic lower bounds establish the inherent difficulty of estimating dynamic effects and minimizing welfare loss. They also reveal that the tension between these goals is fundamental to the studied problem. The contribution therefore combines a configurable design with theoretical benchmarks for what is achievable, specifically in the setting where non-stationarity follows linear trends.
neurips-2023-non-stationary-experimental.tldr: Under linear trends, a configurable experimental design achieves optimal rates or an optimal trade-off between estimating changing effects and limiting welfare loss.

paragraphs: Counterfactual inference asks what would have happened under a different course of events. For continuous outcomes, methods seeking one identified answer can require strong assumptions about the causal model. This paper instead seeks informative intervals of possible counterfactual answers, allowing uncertainty about the underlying model to remain visible.

The authors first prove that continuous differentiability of the causal functions is generally insufficient to make those intervals informative. Their Curvature Sensitivity Model adds a bound on the curvature of the functions' level sets. This restriction enables informative bounds. Existing point-identification methods emerge as special cases when the curvature bound is zero, connecting the proposed sensitivity approach to more restrictive methods.

The paper implements the model through an Augmented Pseudo-Invertible Decoder, a deep generative model combining residual normalizing flows with variational augmentations. Empirical results demonstrate its effectiveness. The contribution is a route to partial counterfactual identification for continuous outcomes in Markovian structural causal models, where informative answers depend on an explicit geometric restriction rather than smoothness alone.
neurips-2023-partial-counterfactual-iden.tldr: Bounding curvature in causal models enables informative intervals for continuous counterfactual outcomes where smoothness alone is insufficient.

paragraphs: Restoring a damaged face image is difficult when the degradation process cannot be modeled precisely. Existing diffusion-based restoration methods often depend on an explicit model of that process. PGDiff takes a different approach by guiding a pretrained diffusion model toward selected properties of high-quality images.

This partial guidance can describe properties such as image structure and color statistics. It is applied during reverse diffusion and combined with the model's diffusion prior. The guidance does not assume a particular degradation process, making the approach more adaptable to complex damage according to the paper. It specifies desirable aspects of the restored result without requiring a full account of how the input was degraded.

The framework can also combine guidance from different restoration tasks to handle composite tasks. Experiments report better results than existing diffusion-prior-based approaches and favorable competitiveness with task-specific models. These findings support using selected output properties as a flexible means of steering restoration across multiple tasks.
neurips-2023-pgdiff-guiding-diffusion-mo.tldr: PGDiff restores faces by guiding pretrained diffusion toward desired image properties without assuming an explicit degradation process.

paragraphs: Visual reinforcement-learning systems can encode distracting details alongside information needed for action. Changes in backgrounds or lighting can then disrupt a learned model even when those details are irrelevant to the task. RePo addresses this by learning a compact representation designed to retain information useful for predicting dynamics and rewards.

Its objective encourages strong prediction while restricting information flowing from images into the latent representation. The reported results show substantially improved resilience to visual distractors in dynamic environments. The paper also identifies a remaining limit: the learned encoder is not invariant to substantial distribution shifts, so resistance to distractors does not eliminate the need for adaptation.

To handle larger shifts, RePo adds a reward-free alignment procedure that adapts the encoder at test time. This allows quick adjustment to substantially different environments without relearning the dynamics model or policy. Simulation results with significant irrelevant visual variation support the combined approach, linking selective representation learning with targeted adaptation when the visual environment changes.
neurips-2023-repo-resilient-model-based-.tldr: RePo limits irrelevant visual information in model-based reinforcement learning and adds reward-free encoder adaptation for larger distribution shifts.

paragraphs: The Koopman operator describes a dynamical system by advancing its observable quantities through time. Learning its eigenvalues and eigenfunctions from data provides a spectral description of the system. This paper develops non-asymptotic learning bounds for those quantities, addressing accuracy at finite sample sizes rather than only eventual convergence.

The analysis focuses on time-reversal-invariant stochastic systems, including Langevin dynamics, and compares Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Reduced Rank Regression. Its bounds combine control of operator-norm estimation error with a new measure of distortion in estimated eigenfunctions. New minimax bounds for the operator-norm error form a central part of the argument.

The results indicate similar variance for the two estimators but greater bias for Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition, which may worsen its learning rate. They also help explain spurious eigenvalues previously observed empirically. Numerical experiments illustrate these implications. The contribution connects finite-data spectral accuracy to both estimation error and eigenfunction distortion within the stated class of dynamical systems.
neurips-2023-sharp-spectral-rates-for-ko.tldr: Finite-sample spectral bounds clarify bias, variance, and spurious eigenvalues in two Koopman estimators for time-reversal-invariant stochastic systems.

paragraphs: Federated learning simulations need datasets divided into groups, and foundation-model scale makes that organization challenging. Dataset Grouper is a library for creating such datasets from existing collections using user-specified partitions. It supports heterogeneous groups that can be used with existing learning frameworks.

The library is designed to scale even when a single group's data cannot fit in memory. It also allows flexibility in choosing both the underlying dataset and how it is partitioned, while remaining independent of a particular framework. These capabilities enable large-scale simulations without tying dataset organization to one training implementation.

Experiments demonstrate federated language modeling on datasets orders of magnitude larger than in previous work, with models containing hundreds of millions or billions of parameters. At this scale, the authors observe algorithms such as FedAvg behaving more like meta-learning methods than empirical risk minimization methods. That finding suggests potential value for downstream personalization and task-specific adaptation, alongside the library's contribution to scalable experimentation.
neurips-2023-towards-federated-foundatio.tldr: Dataset Grouper enables foundation-scale federated simulations and reveals behavior suggesting FedAvg's usefulness for personalization and adaptation.

paragraphs: Recurrent neural networks help researchers investigate possible mechanisms underlying cognition. Training them becomes difficult when a task requires information to persist across long periods. Gating mechanisms can help, but the paper notes that mechanisms such as LSTMs and GRUs lack experimental support for direct comparison with biological neural circuits.

The authors introduce specialized skip connections through time to help task-relevant dynamics develop during training. They subsequently return the network to its original architecture to restore biological plausibility. This separates the architecture used to support learning from the architecture ultimately used as a model of neural computation.

Across the cognitive tasks examined, the approach enables learning that conventional methods find impractical or potentially impossible. It also reduces training steps and elapsed training time, especially for tasks requiring prolonged temporal integration or memory of past events in hidden states. The findings expand the experimental tasks accessible to biologically plausible RNN models, supporting investigation of neural mechanisms for computations with long-term dependencies.
neurips-2023-training-biologically-plaus.tldr: Temporary skip connections through time help biologically plausible RNNs learn long-memory cognitive tasks before returning to their original architecture.

paragraphs: Text embeddings encode language as numerical vectors, but the semantic meaning of their algebraic relationships can be difficult to establish. This paper examines semantic independence: the intuition that concepts such as eggplant and tomato can be independent once the broader concept vegetable is given. The challenge is turning that intuition into a coherent mathematical relation.

The authors begin with independence axioms that a sensible formalization should satisfy. They argue that an algebraic representation of semantic independence should obey those same rules. This leads to partial orthogonality as the relevant structure, and they develop theory and methods demonstrating that it captures semantic independence.

The paper also introduces independence-preserving embeddings, which retain the conditional independence structure of a distribution. It proves that such embeddings and approximations exist. Together, these contributions connect semantic interpretation with formal constraints on vector geometry, while also establishing that embeddings can preserve specified probabilistic independence relationships. This provides a principled basis for studying meaning beyond informal interpretations of vector similarity.
neurips-2023-uncovering-meanings-of-embe.tldr: The paper connects semantic independence to partial orthogonality and proves the existence of embeddings that preserve conditional independence structures.
